seo.title: Reckon
seo.description: Reckon compares what was declared with what is owed, line by line.

name: Reckon

hero.title: What was declared vs what is owed. Spot the difference.
hero.text: A tax return says what a company declared; however, the documents filed show what is owed.

overview: Reckon reads every one of those documents, works out the tax each line should have attracted, and shows the officer where the two disagree: the figure, the document it came from and the tax rule applied.

blocks.title: Most of what is missed was never looked for.
blocks.text: A liability rarely hides in one document. It shows where the general ledger, the bank statement and the return disagree, and those three are seldom put side by side. Reckon compares every line of every document, so a check that takes an officer a week happens in seconds.

figures.label: Reckon / 02
figures.title: Three records, one rule, one exception.
figures.caption: An offshore licence in the ledger and the bank statement; no reverse-charge VAT on the return.

image.alt: General ledger, VAT return and bank statement compared against one rule

blocks.title: Start with what the taxpayer already filed.
blocks.text: Returns, general ledgers, trial balances, financial statements, schedules and bank statements, in PDF, Excel or scanned form. Reckon reads them into one chart of accounts and maps every line to the tax areas it falls under.

figures.label: Reckon / 03
figures.title: One chart of accounts.
figures.caption: Every line tagged to the taxes it attracts: CIT, VAT, WHT, PAYE, CGT, stamp duty, transfer pricing.

image.alt: Source documents harmonised into one chart of accounts

blocks.title: Every line, tested.
blocks.text: For each line Reckon classifies what it is, computes what the applicable rule expects, and compares that with what was declared and what was remitted. A fee posted to the interest ledger is still a fee, and is tested as one. Differences above the materiality threshold for the industry become exceptions.

figures.label: Reckon / 04
figures.title: An exception, as the officer sees it.
figures.caption: Figure, source, rule, and where AI was used to read the input.

image.alt: Exception detail showing figure, source, rule and status

blocks.title: Patterns across years, not just lines.
blocks.text: Reckon keeps the taxpayer’s history as one profile. A series of short agreements that together make one long borrowing, or receipts that reconcile within a year but not across years, are tested as a matter of course.

image.alt: Timeline of three renewed 364-day facilities read as one borrowing

blocks.title: The officer decides.
blocks.text: Reckon raises exceptions; it does not raise findings. Every exception is reviewed by an officer, who raises a finding or dismisses it with a reason. The rules that produce exceptions are configuration the administration maintains itself, so two teams examining the same taxpayer reach the same result. AI is used to read scanned and unstructured input, and the exception says where.

figures.label: Reckon / 06
figures.title: Rules, then judgement.
figures.caption: The administration sets the rules. Reckon applies them. The officer decides.

image.alt: Three columns: the administration sets, Reckon applies, the officer decides

blocks.title: A finding that survives objection.
blocks.text: Each finding keeps the document version, the line, the rule version, the officer’s review and the supervisor’s approval. The same record is produced at reconciliation or before a tribunal, and stays with the case when officers move.

figures.label: Reckon / 07
figures.title: One finding, traced.
figures.caption: Every object in the chain is versioned.

image.alt: Versioned chain from document to finding

blocks.title: One engine. Desk review, audit, investigation.
blocks.text: Desk review runs on every filing as it arrives and clears or escalates it without an officer’s time. Audit takes selected cases through evidence requests, fieldwork and findings. Investigation works at transaction level for enforcement. The rules and the taxpayer record are shared; the workflow, people and depth are not.

figures.label: Reckon / 08
figures.title: Three uses of one engine.
figures.caption: Each tier has its own trigger, scope, officer and output, and draws on the modules it needs.

image.alt: Desk review, audit and investigation tiers sharing one engine

audience.title: Built for those with a mandate to collect.
audience.text: Revenue administrations and large-taxpayer offices, state internal revenue services, tax audit and investigation units, and the audit firms acting for them. Reckon reads from existing systems of record; write-back is approved by a person and logged.
